newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees tax on "callback" phone services.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees tax on "callback" phone services.

text.p: The European Union adopted rules on Monday to allow national governments to tax telephone services offered by foreign companies, a move aimed especially at "callback" services operating in the United States.

The legislation agreed by EU economic and finance ministers would also allow governments to exempt from taxes telecoms services offered by EU companies to customers abroad -- a move the European Commission said was inappropriate.

The initiative was prompted by the growing popularity of services that allow consumers to bypass high European phone charges by dialing a U.S. number and getting called back with an open phone line to make calls at low U.S. rates.
Those calls are not now subject to national value-added taxes (VAT), which range from 15 percent to 25 percent in the EU.

The Commission, responding to a unaminous request from EU governments, proposed that foreign firms be required to charge VAT on telecoms services offered to EU customers -- putting them on a par with their European counterparts.
The EU ministers agreed texts on Monday giving each of the 15 member states a temporary exemption from the EU's existing VAT rules pending adoption of permanent changes to the law.

But they decided to go beyond the Commission's proposal by agreeing that telecoms services should be taxed in the country where they are used rather than in the country of origin, thus exempting services offered outside the EU.
The Commission does not object to that concept in principle, but argues that it should be accomplished by amending the existing law, not through the temporary exemptions, EU officials said.
They said the Commission was also concerned about possible double taxation or non-taxation since not all EU states will change their systems at the same time.
But the ministers pledged in a declaration to change their laws by July 1 and said those acting earlier should take action to avoid double taxation.
The exemptions agreed by the ministers will be valid until the end of 1999 or until the existing VAT rules are revamped. -- Suzanne Perry, Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
